title: Sending an unnecessarily identifiable physical sample to storage
description: The wet lab may transfer the sample with direct identifiers or richer-than-necessary labels attached, making the specimen itself disclosing when moved into storage.
assumptions: Assumes the sample or its container can bear participant identifiers, accession numbers, or other labels visible to handlers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; PA03.02 is used here for disclosure through sharing/transfer of the sample, but the exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Identification via labels or shipment metadata during transfer
description: While the physical sample is being moved to freezer storage, labels, barcodes, chain-of-custody forms, or routing metadata on the container may identify the data subject or make them identifiable to staff involved in transport.
assumptions: Assumes the transfer involves visible labels, paperwork, or tracking metadata accessible to personnel beyond the minimum necessary.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; used here for observing/deriving identity from metadata associated with the transferred sample.

title: Linkability of the sample to other records during transit
description: Persistent sample IDs, barcodes, or freezer intake paperwork used on the flow can allow the specimen to be linked with laboratory records, consent files, or clinical datasets, enabling correlation across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers are reused across systems or paperwork accompanying the sample.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for cross-context linking may vary.

title: Overexposure of stored sample information within the storage facility
description: On receipt, the storage function may retain the sample in a way that exposes labels, location logs, or inventory entries to more personnel than necessary, disclosing participant-related information.
assumptions: Assumes freezer storage includes inventory systems, rack maps, or visible labels accessible to staff.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is best-effort; PA03.09 is used for internal exposure/access during storage handling.

title: Stored sample becomes linkable across studies or repositories
description: The storage destination may index the sample under a persistent identifier that enables linking this specimen with other samples, studies, or participant records beyond the original storage purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the storage inventory supports reuse of identifiers or cross-reference with external datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for indexing/linking in storage may differ.

title: Use of the stored sample beyond the expected storage purpose
description: After receipt, the storage facility may enable later access, retrieval, or secondary use of the physical sample that goes beyond the purpose understood when it was sent for storage.
assumptions: Assumes governance or access controls may permit later retrieval/use for additional testing, sharing, or research.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; used here for secondary use/function creep enabled by storage.

title: Wet lab can relink the de-identified sample ID to an individual or case
description: Although the flow carries a de-identified ID, the wet lab may possess local context, accession logs, collection timing, or physical sample handling records that allow the identifier to be linked back to a person or case.
assumptions: Wet Lab retains side information about sample collection or handling that can be correlated with the returned ID.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; mapped to a relinking/re-identification style action based on context.

title: Identifier disclosure in transit exposes sample association metadata
description: If the de-identified ID is intercepted on the flow, an observer may learn that a particular sample exists and is being processed between LIMS and the wet lab, and may capture the identifier for later correlation with other systems or events.
assumptions: The transport channel or surrounding operational metadata is observable by an unauthorized party.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; used here for disclosure/observation of data in transit.

title: Flow metadata enables linkage across systems despite de-identification
description: Even if the payload contains only a de-identified ID, message timing, sender/recipient identities, batch structure, and repeated identifier use can enable linking records across LIMS and wet-lab workflows, undermining separation between identities and samples.
assumptions: An observer or participating system can access communication metadata or repeated identifiers across transactions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to PANOPTIC linkage/correlation behavior; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Wet lab infers sensitive attributes from the returned sample identifier and context
description: Receipt of the de-identified ID, combined with specimen type, workflow stage, ordering context, or project information already known to the wet lab, may allow inference of sensitive health, study-participation, or case-related information about the data subject.
assumptions: Wet Lab has contextual knowledge beyond the identifier itself.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; mapped to inference from contextualized data.

title: LIMS may share the identifier without sufficient purpose limitation or minimization
description: Returning the de-identified ID to the wet lab may exceed what is strictly necessary if the wet lab could operate with a more limited token, one-time alias, or workflow-specific reference. Over-sharing can create unnecessary privacy risk even when direct identifiers are absent.
assumptions: A less linkable or more limited identifier could feasibly support the wet-lab task.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for unnecessary sharing/minimization concerns; exact id uncertain.

title: Sharing raw sequence data may disclose identifiable genetic information
description: The wet lab sends raw sequence data that can inherently contain uniquely identifying genetic markers or sensitive health-related information about a person. The act of transmitting the full raw dataset to storage increases the chance that identifiable or sensitive attributes are exposed beyond the minimum necessary.
assumptions: Sequence data is human-derived or otherwise attributable to an individual or small cohort, and is stored with enough fidelity to preserve identifying variants.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort; exact mapping for disclosure of genomic data may differ.

title: Transfer metadata may enable linkage of sequence data to a specific subject or experiment
description: Even if the payload is stored as raw sequence files, metadata observable on the flow—such as file names, sample identifiers, project codes, timestamps, sender/receiver context, or run identifiers—may allow linking the dataset to a particular person, specimen, study, or clinical event.
assumptions: Operational metadata accompanies or can be inferred from the transfer, and identifiers or quasi-identifiers are present in naming conventions or transport logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; this is primarily a linkage threat arising from transfer metadata rather than payload content alone.

title: Flow observability may reveal the existence of a sequencing event for an individual
description: Observation of the transfer itself may let an attacker or unauthorized insider infer that sequencing has occurred for a given sample, patient, or study participant. This can identify involvement in testing or research even without reading the full data contents.
assumptions: An observer can monitor network traffic, job scheduling, or transfer logs and correlate the event with a person, sample intake, or experiment timeline.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate; threat concerns identifiability from the existence of the transfer.

title: Stored raw sequence data may later be linked across datasets or projects
description: Once the cluster filesystem receives and stores raw sequence data, the destination may retain it in a way that enables future correlation with other files, metadata, or external datasets. Genomic data is especially linkable across contexts, increasing the risk of cross-project or cross-subject linkage.
assumptions: The filesystem or surrounding environment permits aggregation, indexing, or reuse of stored sequence files and associated metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity for downstream linkage at storage may vary.

title: Retention of full raw sequence files may enable excessive disclosure
description: The cluster filesystem may store the complete raw sequence dataset longer than necessary or with broader accessibility than intended. Because raw sequence files can reveal extensive sensitive information, storage at the destination can create disclosure risk through later access, copying, backup, or secondary use.
assumptions: The destination retains raw data, potentially in backups or shared storage areas, and access controls or retention limits may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; threat is destination-side disclosure through storage and retention practices.

title: Storage may enable use of sequence data beyond the original expected purpose
description: After receipt, the cluster filesystem environment may make raw sequence data available for analytics, sharing, or reuse beyond the purpose originally expected by the data subject or sample provider. This creates a risk that the data is processed in ways that are not transparent or reasonably anticipated.
assumptions: Stored data can be accessed by downstream tools, users, or projects without strict purpose limitation enforcement.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity for secondary use/purpose expansion may differ.

title: Over-disclosure of raw sequence data to compute nodes
description: The cluster filesystem may provide full raw sequence datasets to compute nodes even when only a subset or derived features are necessary for the intended computation, exposing more personal/genetic information than required.
assumptions: Raw sequence data can contain personal or sensitive genomic information and jobs may not always require the complete dataset.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; mapped to a generic disclose/share action because exact PANOPTIC taxonomy is not provided.

title: Identification through raw sequence data in transit
description: Digital raw sequence data transmitted from the cluster filesystem to compute nodes may itself contain uniquely identifying genomic patterns, enabling identification of a data subject if intercepted or otherwise exposed during transfer.
assumptions: The transfer path or intermediate infrastructure could be observed by unauthorized parties, and genomic data is sufficiently distinctive to identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to data transfer/transmission; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Linkability via repeated dataset transfers and metadata
description: Transfer metadata such as dataset identifiers, job identifiers, timestamps, node assignments, or sample references can allow observers or internal actors to link multiple processing events to the same individual, sample, or study across runs.
assumptions: Operational metadata accompanies or can be inferred from the transfer and is visible to some parties beyond the minimum necessary set.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to transmission activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Secondary use of raw sequence data on compute nodes
description: Once compute nodes receive the raw sequence data, software, users, or scheduled jobs on those nodes may process, copy, or retain the data for purposes beyond the objective-specific transformation originally intended.
assumptions: Compute environments may be multi-tenant, support reusable storage, or permit operators and workflows broad access to received data.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; mapped to use/process after collection/receipt.

title: Processing on compute nodes beyond data subjects' expectations or consent
description: Objective-specific transformation on compute nodes may exceed the scope understood by data subjects or the permissions attached to the sequence data, especially if workflows perform additional analyses or generate extra inferences.
assumptions: The lawful/authorized scope for genomic processing is narrower than all technically possible analyses on the compute nodes.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping of non-compliance to downstream processing activity; exact PANOPTIC id uncertain.

title: Detectability of sensitive traits from received raw sequence data
description: Compute nodes processing raw sequence data can derive or expose highly sensitive attributes, such as ancestry, familial relationships, or health-related variants, making the presence of such traits detectable to operators or other unauthorized parties with access to outputs, logs, or memory.
assumptions: Compute-node environments or tooling may expose intermediate results, logs, or memory artifacts to parties not strictly authorized for those inferences.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is best-effort to analysis/inference activity; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Over-disclosure of research data when exporting to delivery zone
description: The cluster filesystem may send more context-relevant research data than is necessary for delivery, including extra attributes, intermediate results, or embedded identifiers, increasing disclosure risk once the data is staged in the DMZ.
assumptions: The generated research data may still contain direct or indirect identifiers or unnecessary fields not strictly required for delivery.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; PA03.02 is used here to represent disclosure/sharing of data to another zone.

title: Identifiability from data in transit and transfer metadata
description: Even if the payload is intended for delivery, the transferred dataset or its metadata (file names, paths, timestamps, project labels, cohort names, transfer size/frequency) may enable identification of data subjects or inference about a specific study population during transit.
assumptions: The flow may expose meaningful metadata to infrastructure components or logs beyond the payload itself.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate; PA01.01 is used as a best-fit for identification/inference from transferred data or metadata.

title: Linkability via repeated transfers to the DMZ
description: Repeated movement of similarly structured research datasets to the DMZ can allow observers or receiving processes to correlate files across deliveries, linking records, projects, or cohorts over time even when each individual transfer appears limited.
assumptions: Transfer events, naming conventions, or stable pseudonyms may persist across deliveries.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; chosen as a best-fit for correlation/linking across transfer events.

title: Excessive exposure in the delivery DMZ
description: Once received in the data delivery DMZ, the dataset may be stored or made available in a location accessible to more users, systems, or delivery mechanisms than intended, causing broader disclosure of sensitive research data.
assumptions: The DMZ is designed for onward delivery and may have broader accessibility or weaker minimization controls than the source filesystem.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action PA03.09 is a best-effort estimate for making data available/disclosing it onward in a delivery context.

title: Unawareness of onward delivery or exposure conditions
description: Data subjects may be unaware that context-relevant research data is staged in a delivery DMZ, potentially under different access, retention, or onward-sharing conditions than in the originating research environment.
assumptions: The delivery DMZ may constitute a distinct processing context not fully reflected in notices or governance artifacts communicated to data subjects.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate; PA04.01 is used as a best-fit for insufficient transparency/awareness.

title: Processing in the DMZ beyond the original research-delivery purpose
description: After receipt, the data delivery DMZ may retain, index, transform, or repurpose the research data for operational convenience, troubleshooting, or secondary sharing in ways that are incompatible with the original purpose limitation for generating the dataset.
assumptions: The DMZ may perform additional storage, indexing, or operational processing beyond simple pass-through delivery.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; PA04.03 is used as an approximate fit for non-compliant secondary processing or purpose expansion.

title: Excessive sample-request details disclose participant information
description: When the NCCoE Researcher submits a physical sample request, the request may include more participant-related detail than necessary (e.g., direct identifiers, rich case context, or unnecessary study metadata). This disclosure at the source can expose sensitive information about the individual tied to the requested sample.
assumptions: Assumes the request can contain participant identifiers or detailed contextual metadata beyond a minimal specimen locator and authorization data.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; likely corresponds to a request/share/disclose action but exact id may differ.

title: Request metadata can link researcher activity to specific samples or participants
description: Even if the request payload is limited, metadata on the flow (request timing, requester identity, specimen identifiers, project or protocol references) can enable linking a researcher, study, and specific sample or participant across systems or logs.
assumptions: Assumes transport, middleware, or operational logs retain request metadata and specimen references.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; intended to capture transmission/observation of metadata enabling linkage.

title: Sample request may reveal participant identity through identifiers in transit
description: If the physical sample request contains participant names, medical record numbers, coded specimen IDs that are readily resolvable, or other identifying attributes, interception or broad visibility of the flow can identify the individual associated with the sample.
assumptions: Assumes the request traverses infrastructure where network traces, application logs, or message queues may be accessible to parties beyond the minimum need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Tree node and PANOPTIC id are best-effort approximations for identification via data in transit.

title: DNA Store can link request records with inventory and participant records
description: Upon receipt, the DNA Store may correlate the incoming request with specimen inventory, participant records, prior requests, and study information, enabling broader linkage of the participant and researcher activity than necessary for fulfillment.
assumptions: Assumes the DNA Store maintains inventory, chain-of-custody, participant mapping, or request history records that can be cross-referenced.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; intended to capture recipient-side correlation/linking.

title: DNA Store may retain unnecessary request data
description: The DNA Store may store the full physical sample request, including requester identity, participant identifiers, justification text, and protocol details, longer than necessary or in broader-access repositories, increasing privacy exposure.
assumptions: Assumes request records are logged or archived for operations, audit, or fulfillment tracking.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is best-effort for recipient-side storage/retention.

title: Secondary use of request information beyond sample fulfillment
description: Information in the physical sample request could be used by the DNA Store for purposes beyond fulfilling the request, such as operational analytics, researcher profiling, or unrelated inventory analyses, without the participant's or requester's expectation.
assumptions: Assumes governance does not strictly limit downstream use of request metadata and contents.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; mapped to recipient-side use/processing beyond the original purpose.

title: Insufficient transparency or policy basis for processing request-linked participant data
description: The DNA Store's processing of participant-linked information in the request may lack clear notice, documented purpose limitation, or demonstrable policy/legal basis, creating a non-compliance risk when handling sensitive biospecimen-related data.
assumptions: Assumes the request includes or can be linked to participant-related data subject to policy, consent, or regulatory constraints.
uncertainty_note: Exact PANOPTIC id is uncertain; mapped to recipient-side collection/processing under governance obligations.

title: Over-disclosure of physical sample beyond the requested scope
description: The DNA Store may release a physical sample containing more material or richer identifying content than is necessary for the specific research request, exposing unnecessary personal or genetic information to the researcher.
assumptions: The sample is linked or linkable to an individual and only a subset or controlled aliquot would be sufficient for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for physical sample release/minimization may differ.

title: Unauthorized release of physical sample by the DNA Store
description: The DNA Store could provide the physical sample to a researcher whose authorization, project approval, or purpose limitation is invalid, expired, or broader than permitted, resulting in an impermissible disclosure.
assumptions: Access decisions depend on governance, consent, ethics approval, or role-based authorization checks at the DNA Store.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for authorization checking during sample release is uncertain.

title: Identification through shipment or handling metadata
description: Even if the sample container uses coded identifiers, metadata on the transfer path such as labels, chain-of-custody records, pickup timing, storage location, or request references may enable identification of the data subject associated with the sample.
assumptions: Transfer involves labels, logs, or handling records accessible to personnel beyond the minimum necessary set.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; using a generic transfer/handling metadata activity because no reference material is provided.

title: Linkability of sample transfers across studies or requests
description: Consistent sample codes, request identifiers, or chain-of-custody metadata may allow observers or recipients to link this physical sample transfer with other transfers, datasets, or study activities concerning the same individual or cohort.
assumptions: Stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers are reused across requests or systems.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; exact sub-activity id for physical transfer metadata/linkage is uncertain.

title: Secondary use of the physical sample by the researcher
description: After receipt, the NCCoE Researcher may use the physical sample for analyses, retention, or sharing beyond the approved purpose of the original request, disclosing sensitive genetic or biological information in ways not expected by the data subject.
assumptions: The researcher has technical ability to derive additional information from the sample and downstream controls may be limited.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for downstream use/processing after receipt; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Use of the sample inconsistent with consent or policy constraints
description: The researcher may process or retain the physical sample in a manner that conflicts with the individual's consent, ethics approval, or institutional policy, such as prohibited analyses or retention beyond allowed periods.
assumptions: Consent and policy constraints exist and are not automatically enforced at the point of use.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for consent/policy-constrained use is uncertain.

title: Insufficient accountability for sample receipt and use
description: If receipt, custody changes, and subsequent use of the physical sample are not adequately logged or attributable, the researcher could later deny having received, accessed, or used the sample in a particular way, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Audit logging or chain-of-custody controls may be incomplete or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; mapped to post-receipt handling/use due to lack of reference material.

title: Identifiability from labeled or uniquely associated physical sample in transit
description: The physical sample or its packaging may carry direct identifiers, coded identifiers, or unique characteristics that allow the sample to be tied to a specific individual during transport between the researcher and receiving clerk.
assumptions: Assumes the sample container, requisition, or shipping materials include participant identifiers or stable codes linkable to a participant.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for physical sample transfer/labeling may vary.

title: Linkability via shipment metadata and sample codes
description: Courier records, chain-of-custody forms, tracking numbers, timestamps, sender/recipient details, and sample accession codes may enable linking this sample movement to other records about the same participant or study involvement.
assumptions: Assumes logistics metadata or accession identifiers are retained and can be correlated with laboratory or study systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Detectability of participant involvement from observable sample transfer
description: Observation of the shipment, package markings, sender/recipient names, or handling context may reveal that a person is participating in a sequencing-related research activity even if the sample contents are not opened.
assumptions: Assumes the package or transfer context exposes study, institution, or specimen-related information to transport personnel or bystanders.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; detectability here is based on observable transfer metadata and packaging.

title: Excessive disclosure by the sender when preparing the sample for transfer
description: The researcher may include more participant information than necessary on the sample, requisition, or accompanying paperwork, increasing the amount of personal data exposed during handoff and transport.
assumptions: Assumes the sender controls labeling and accompanying documentation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; tree node is approximate for over-disclosure at disclosure time.

title: Disclosure from insecure receipt and handling at the receiving clerk
description: On receipt, the clerk may leave the sample or paperwork unattended, visible, or accessible to unauthorized personnel, exposing participant-related information contained on the sample or accompanying documents.
assumptions: Assumes the receiving area is shared or not strictly access-controlled.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort for receipt/handling/storage on intake.

title: Linkability created by intake logging and accessioning
description: The receiving clerk may log the incoming sample together with shipment details, study identifiers, or participant codes in a way that enables linking the sample to other datasets or prior submissions.
assumptions: Assumes intake systems or manual logs retain stable identifiers and contextual metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id for accessioning/logging is approximate.

title: Identification through recipient-side matching of sample and paperwork
description: The receiving clerk or downstream lab intake process may combine the sample with requisitions, manifests, or existing records to identify the participant associated with the specimen.
assumptions: Assumes the recipient has access to auxiliary records or identifiers sufficient for re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Excessive disclosure on the sample request form
description: The clinician may include more personal or clinical detail on the physical sample request form than is necessary for the patient to carry out the sample collection/submission, exposing sensitive health information to the patient in a context where only limited instructions were needed.
assumptions: Assumes the form can contain detailed clinical indications, identifiers, or other sensitive notes beyond the minimum necessary for sample collection.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; likely corresponds to a disclose/share action in a care workflow, but exact id may differ.

title: Identifiability from visible form contents during handover
description: Because the request is physically handed to the patient, names, identifiers, test type, clinic branding, or specialty information visible on the form can directly identify the patient and reveal that they are undergoing a particular medical test.
assumptions: Assumes the form is readable by nearby persons during handover or transport by the patient.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for physical transmission/exposure; exact sub-activity id is uncertain.

title: Linkability via persistent identifiers on the request form
description: The form may carry persistent identifiers such as patient name, medical record number, barcode, accession number, or clinician details that allow the sample request to be linked with other records, visits, or later laboratory processing steps.
assumptions: Assumes the request form includes stable identifiers reused across systems or encounters.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; threat is grounded in the transfer of a labeled request artifact.

title: Disclosure of sensitive disease or test inference from the request artifact
description: Even without reading full details, the type of requested test, department name, or specimen instructions on the form may let others infer sensitive conditions, genetic testing intent, or other private health facts about the patient.
assumptions: Assumes the form or envelope visibly indicates the nature of the requested testing or specialty service.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id uncertain.

title: Patient may be unable to prove what information was provided
description: If there is no receipt, copy, or audit trail of the exact request form handed over, the patient may later be unable to demonstrate what instructions, identifiers, or disclosures were included, hindering dispute resolution or accountability.
assumptions: Assumes the handover is informal and no duplicate copy or logging mechanism is retained by the patient.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate; this is a best-effort fit to receipt/record-related activity.

title: Patient disclosure of identity through provision of physical sample
description: By providing a physical sample that is retrieved by the clinician, the patient discloses personal and often highly sensitive health-related information that can directly or indirectly identify them.
assumptions: The sample is labeled, linked to a request, or otherwise associated with the patient identity or clinical context.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; exact sub-activity for physical handover/retrieval of a specimen may differ.

title: Identifiability via sample labels and contextual metadata during transfer
description: Even if the sample contents are not examined in transit, labels, barcodes, timestamps, location, and the fact that a clinician retrieves a sample for a specific request can make the patient identifiable.
assumptions: The physical sample container or accompanying paperwork contains identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or request metadata visible during handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping; PANOPTIC id for metadata observation during physical transfer is approximate.

title: Linkability of patient to condition or episode through sample-request association
description: The sample can be linked to a specific patient, encounter, clinician, test request, or treatment pathway, enabling correlation across records or events beyond what is necessary for the immediate retrieval.
assumptions: A request identifier, accession number, or other persistent reference accompanies the sample and can be correlated with other systems or logs.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate because the exact sub-activity taxonomy for cross-context linkage of specimen metadata is uncertain.

title: Excessive disclosure from clinician inspection or handling of the sample
description: Upon receipt, the clinician may learn more than necessary from the sample itself or its accompanying information, such as sensitive diagnoses, genetic implications, or other attributes not required for the immediate purpose.
assumptions: The clinician has access to the sample, labels, and associated request details, and purpose limitation or minimization controls may be weak.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for recipient-side examination/use of a physical specimen.

title: Collection or use of the physical sample without valid consent or compatible legal basis
description: The clinician's retrieval and subsequent use of the sample may occur without the patient's informed consent, outside the originally understood purpose, or without another appropriate legal basis.
assumptions: Consent, notice, or legal basis for retrieval and downstream use may be absent, unclear, or broader than the patient's expectations.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; exact sub-activity for consent/authorization failure in specimen retrieval is uncertain.

title: Unawareness of downstream handling of the retrieved sample
description: The patient may be unaware of how the clinician will store, analyze, share, or retain the retrieved sample after collection, reducing transparency and the patient's ability to exercise control.
assumptions: Transparency notices about specimen handling, retention, secondary use, or onward sharing are incomplete or not effectively communicated.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for transparency/awareness issues in specimen handling.

title: Insufficient evidence of sample retrieval and handling actions
description: If retrieval and chain-of-custody actions are not properly logged, the clinician or organization may later be unable to demonstrate what happened to the sample, undermining accountability and the patient's ability to challenge misuse.
assumptions: Audit logging or chain-of-custody controls for physical specimen retrieval are incomplete or unreliable.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate for accountability gaps around physical sample custody.

title: Over-disclosure of patient identity or excess context on the sample/package
description: The clinician may send the physical sample with direct identifiers or more contextual information than the sequencing lab needs, enabling the receiving clerk to identify the patient unnecessarily from labels, requisitions, or accompanying paperwork.
assumptions: The sequencing workflow could operate with a coded specimen and limited metadata rather than full identity details at intake.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping: likely a disclosure/sharing sub-activity, but the exact PA03.xx code may differ.

title: Identifiability from labels, chain-of-custody data, or shipment metadata in transit
description: Even before laboratory processing, the sample container, courier paperwork, routing details, timestamps, and sender/recipient information can make the data subject identifiable or strongly inferable to parties handling the shipment.
assumptions: The sample is physically transported with labels or logistics metadata visible to intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; intended to capture observation of identifying metadata during transfer.

title: Linkability of the specimen to other records via persistent specimen identifiers
description: A stable specimen ID, accession precursor, barcode, or paperwork number on the physical sample may allow intermediaries or later recipients to link this sample to other clinical or research records about the same person.
assumptions: Identifiers on the sample or accompanying documents are reused across systems or can be correlated with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact sub-activity id may vary.

title: Exposure of sensitive attributes from the nature of the specimen or accompanying notes
description: The specimen type, collection context, clinic specialty, or notes attached during transport may disclose sensitive health information, research participation, or suspected conditions to transport or intake personnel who do not need that level of detail.
assumptions: The package or paperwork reveals specimen type, ordering department, diagnosis hints, or study context.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is approximate; used here for exposure during transfer.

title: Linking the received sample with existing patient or study records at intake
description: On receipt, the clerk may correlate the specimen and its identifiers with existing laboratory, hospital, or study-management records, increasing the ability to build a richer profile of the data subject than necessary for initial intake.
assumptions: The receiving clerk has access to multiple systems or paperwork sources that can be cross-referenced.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to a collection/aggregation activity; exact id may differ.

title: Unnecessary disclosure to intake personnel at the sequencing lab
description: The receiving clerk may view patient identity, clinical context, or study details that are not required for their role, causing privacy harm at the destination through role-inappropriate access during specimen intake.
assumptions: Role-based minimization is possible and the clerk does not need full patient context to receive the sample.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is approximate; intended to capture destination-side viewing/handling of received information.

title: Processing the sample beyond the patient's expected or consented research context
description: After receipt, the specimen may be accepted and routed for sequencing or related handling that exceeds the scope the patient understood or consented to, especially if intake does not verify permitted uses and restrictions.
assumptions: Use restrictions or consent directives exist and may not be fully enforced at intake.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping to downstream use/processing at receipt; exact PA id uncertain.

title: Excessive detail in digital sample request reveals unnecessary personal or case information

description: Residual identifiers on the physical sample, container, or disposal documentation may allow the discarded specimen to be linked with laboratory, clinical, or operational records, revealing associations about the individual even after retention requirements are met.
assumptions: The disposal process preserves stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers long enough for later correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; linkage risk depends on how disposal containers and logs are labeled and retained.

title: Disposal reveals sensitive information about the individual or sample context
description: The nature of the sample being discarded, its labeling, or disposal categorization may disclose sensitive facts such as medical condition, testing context, or participation in a study to personnel who can access the disposal item or records.
assumptions: Sample type, hazard class, department, study code, or other contextual markings are visible to disposal handlers or observers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for disposal activity; disclosure may occur through labels or handling context rather than the specimen contents alone.

title: Sample is retained or repurposed instead of being irreversibly disposed
description: Although the flow is intended to dispose of the remainder sample, the destination may store, recover, or otherwise process the specimen for a purpose incompatible with the original expectation, undermining the subject's understanding that retention has ended.
assumptions: Controls do not guarantee irreversible destruction and permit later access, retrieval, or secondary use of the sample.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; exact threat depends on whether the disposal item is a true destruction endpoint or an intermediate holding store.

title: Disposal occurs contrary to retention, consent, or policy constraints
description: The sample may be disposed of before all legal, contractual, research, or subject-directed retention conditions are actually satisfied, creating a privacy-relevant non-compliance issue around lifecycle governance of the specimen.
assumptions: Applicable retention schedules, consent terms, litigation holds, or subject rights may impose conditions not fully enforced at disposal time.
uncertainty_note: This is a governance-focused threat on the disposal step; PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Residual biological material on reused flow cell may disclose prior sample information
description: If the used flow cell is not effectively cleaned before storage or reuse, residual physical sample material may remain and be accessible during a later sequencing run or inspection, disclosing information about the prior data subject's sample.
assumptions: The flow cell can retain recoverable biological residue after a run, and later handlers or processes could access or derive information from that residue.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort; exact mapping for inadequate sanitization/cleaning of physical remnants may differ.

title: Residual sample remnants on the flow cell may enable linkage between sequencing runs
description: Material left on a reused flow cell could allow a later run, operator, or downstream analysis to associate remnants from a previous sample with a new sample or sequencing event, linking otherwise separate processing contexts.
assumptions: Residual material is distinguishable enough to correlate with a prior run or sample identity.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort LINDDUN mapping; linkage here depends on the feasibility of correlating residual material across runs.

title: Residual sample on the flow cell may reveal the identity of the prior sample source
description: If biological remnants remain on the used flow cell, they may contain uniquely identifying genetic material or labels that permit identification of the individual or specimen associated with the previous sequencing run.
assumptions: The residual material or associated markings are sufficient to identify a person or uniquely identify a specimen.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; identification risk depends on the amount and quality of residual material and any associated metadata.

title: Improper retention of sample remnants on the flow cell may exceed the intended processing purpose
description: Leaving physical sample remnants on the used flow cell after the sequencing run can result in continued storage and possible reuse of personal biological material beyond the original sequencing purpose, undermining purpose limitation and data minimization expectations.
assumptions: The original intended purpose did not include retaining residual biological material after run completion.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC and LINDDUN Pro mapping for non-compliance arising from failure to sanitize or dispose of residual sample material.

title: Disclosure of sensitive genomic or research-derived attributes when writing derived data to shared storage
description: Compute Nodes generate context-relevant research data from raw sequence data and send it to the Cluster Filesystem. If the derived dataset still contains identifiable or sensitive genomic variants, phenotypic signals, or subject-linked research attributes, the act of writing it to shared storage can disclose personal information beyond what is necessary for the processing purpose.
assumptions: Derived research data may remain personal or quasi-identifiable, and the cluster filesystem may be accessible to multiple jobs, users, or administrative roles.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for transforming/producing and sharing derived research data; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Identifiability from data-in-transit or transfer metadata
description: During transfer from Compute Nodes to the Cluster Filesystem, the payload or associated metadata such as file names, directory paths, job identifiers, sample identifiers, timestamps, or project labels may directly or indirectly identify a data subject, cohort, or study participant.
assumptions: Transport or storage protocols, logs, or orchestration layers may expose metadata even if payload protections exist.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is a best-fit estimate for collection/observation of identifying metadata in the transfer context.

title: Linkability through persistent identifiers and repeated transfer patterns
description: Repeated writes of sequence-derived research outputs to the filesystem may use stable sample IDs, subject pseudonyms, run IDs, or consistent folder structures. These can enable linking this flow's data with other datasets, prior runs, or external records, revealing that multiple records relate to the same individual or study subject.
assumptions: Identifiers or stable metadata are reused across workflows, projects, or time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for linking via persistent identifiers and workflow metadata.

title: Overexposure of derived research data within the cluster filesystem
description: Once received, the Cluster Filesystem may store the context-relevant research data in locations readable by other tenants, researchers, service accounts, backup systems, or administrators. Broad permissions, inherited ACLs, snapshots, or replication can disclose sensitive derived data to parties not intended for this processing step.
assumptions: The filesystem is shared infrastructure with multi-user or multi-service access paths.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC action is best-effort for storage/dissemination on shared infrastructure.

title: Linkability created by aggregation of derived outputs at the destination
description: The Cluster Filesystem can aggregate this derived dataset with other stored files, logs, and project artifacts. Co-location and indexing at the destination may enable linking records across experiments, timepoints, or modalities, increasing the ability to correlate data back to the same participant or family.
assumptions: The destination supports search, indexing, or structured organization across multiple datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for aggregation/linking at storage destination.

title: Inference of participant traits from stored context-relevant research data
description: Even if direct identifiers are absent, the Cluster Filesystem stores derived research data that may permit inference of disease status, ancestry, familial relationships, or other sensitive traits when analyzed alone or in combination with other stored datasets.
assumptions: Derived sequence-based research outputs retain enough signal for sensitive inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for inference enabled by retained derived data at rest.

title: Processing or retention of derived data beyond participant expectations or stated purpose
description: After receipt, the Cluster Filesystem may retain the context-relevant research data longer than necessary or make it available for secondary analysis, backup, replication, or future reuse that is not aligned with the original participant notice, consent, or governance constraints.
assumptions: Retention, backup, and secondary-use controls may not be tightly coupled to participant-specific permissions or study governance.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping is approximate for purpose/retention non-compliance at the storage destination.

title: Oversharing of sensitive clinical report content to the portal
description: The bioinformaticist may upload a final clinical report containing more personal or sensitive data than is necessary for the portal's intended purpose, increasing disclosure risk at the moment of sharing.
assumptions: Assumes the portal does not require every data element present in the full report and that minimization controls may be weak or manual.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; likely corresponds to a disclose/share action but exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Identification via report metadata in transit
description: Metadata accompanying the uploaded clinical report, such as patient identifiers, case numbers, clinician names, timestamps, or portal account context, could directly identify the data subject or associated staff while the data is in transit.
assumptions: Assumes transport or intermediary systems expose or log metadata beyond strictly necessary routing information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for transmission/upload activity.

title: Linkability of patient cases across uploads
description: Repeated uploads of final clinical reports to the same portal may enable linking multiple submissions to the same patient, family, clinician, or laboratory context through stable identifiers, filenames, accession numbers, or timing patterns.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or recognizable quasi-identifiers are present in payload or transport metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort at a generic linkability level; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity id may vary.

title: Unauthorized disclosure from portal-side access or storage
description: Once the final clinical report is received, the 3rd Party Portal may expose it to unauthorized internal users, external tenants, or downstream recipients through weak access controls, insecure storage, or excessive onward sharing.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores the report and makes it accessible to users or integrated systems.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC destination-side processing/storage action is best-effort.

title: Secondary use of clinical report beyond the original purpose
description: The portal operator may process the uploaded clinical report for analytics, service improvement, model training, profiling, or other purposes not expected by the patient or sending organization.
assumptions: Assumes contractual or technical controls do not fully prevent repurposing by the third party.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for use/processing after collection.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent alignment for third-party portal processing
description: Data subjects may not be adequately informed, or their permissions may not clearly cover storage and processing of the final clinical report by this third-party portal, creating a consent and notice gap.
assumptions: Assumes the portal is a distinct third party and patient-facing notice/consent may not explicitly mention this recipient and its processing.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; this is a best-effort mapping to recipient-side collection/receipt and governance activity.

title: Insufficient evidence of upload receipt, access, or onward disclosure
description: If the portal lacks reliable audit trails, it may be difficult to prove which report version was uploaded, who accessed it, whether it was altered, or whether it was further disclosed, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant events.
assumptions: Assumes audit logging, integrity protection, or retention of access records may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping; exact non-repudiation tree node may differ in a fuller catalog.

title: Portal discloses final clinical report to an unintended counselor account
description: If the 3rd Party Portal associates the report with the wrong user, wrong patient context, or overly broad access group, the act of making the final clinical report available for download can disclose sensitive genetic and clinical information to a counselor who is not authorized for that patient.
assumptions: The portal stores reports for multiple patients and/or multiple counselors and enforces access control at download time.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for portal sharing/disclosure; exact sub-activity id may differ.

title: Download transaction metadata can identify patient involvement in genetic testing
description: Even if the report contents are protected, metadata on the download flow—such as portal endpoint, patient/report identifiers in URLs, timestamps, file names, or session-linked request parameters—may identify a specific patient or reveal that a person is involved in genetic testing or counseling.
assumptions: Network, application, or logging layers expose request metadata beyond the minimum necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for collection/use of identifying metadata during transfer.

title: Portal download metadata enables linkage across encounters or systems
description: Stable report IDs, patient identifiers, counselor account identifiers, or consistent file naming conventions in the transfer can allow observers or integrated systems to link this report download with other visits, tests, or records, building a broader profile of the patient or counselor.
assumptions: Identifiers or quasi-identifiers are reused across transactions or visible to intermediaries/logging systems.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate; linkage via transfer metadata is inferred from common portal download patterns.

title: Downloaded report is stored or handled insecurely by the Genetic Counselor
description: After download, the Genetic Counselor process may save the final clinical report to local storage, shared drives, email, or case-management tools without adequate access restrictions, causing unauthorized disclosure of highly sensitive genetic findings.
assumptions: The counselor workflow includes local caching, onward sharing, or integration into other systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping for downstream use/storage after receipt.

title: Report is used beyond the patient-expected clinical purpose
description: Once downloaded, the final clinical report could be reused for secondary purposes—such as training, broader case discussion, administrative review, or non-essential sharing—without the patient's awareness or expectation, undermining intervenability and control over genetic information.
assumptions: The counselor or connected systems can repurpose the report outside the immediate counseling/treatment context.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN mapping is best-effort; this is framed as loss of user control/intervenability rather than pure policy non-compliance.

title: Insufficient auditability of who downloaded or accessed the final report
description: If the receiving process does not maintain reliable logs tying the downloaded report to the counselor identity, patient context, and access time, it may be impossible to later prove who accessed the report or investigate inappropriate access, weakening accountability for sensitive genetic data handling.
assumptions: Audit logging at or after receipt may be incomplete, mutable, or not retained.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is approximate for access/use logging and accountability activities.

title: Over-disclosure of context-relevant clinical/genetic data to the clinician
description: The Genetic Counselor may make more research/clinical context available than is necessary for the Clinician's immediate purpose, exposing sensitive genetic or related contextual information beyond data minimization expectations.
assumptions: The clinician does not need the full underlying context-relevant dataset for every retrieval or decision.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; mapped to a disclose/share action without source material.

title: Linkability via flow metadata between counselor, clinician, and patient context
description: Even if payload access is controlled, metadata about this transfer or retrieval availability event may allow linking a patient case across the Genetic Counselor and Clinician contexts, especially because genetic/research-related interactions are distinctive.
assumptions: Transport, audit, or workflow metadata is observable to internal systems or logs.
uncertainty_note: Tree node and PANOPTIC mapping are best-effort based on metadata-enabled linking during sharing.

title: Identifiability from context-rich genetic/research data in transit
description: The data made available for clinician retrieval may contain direct or quasi-identifiers, and the combination of genetic findings with clinical context can make the patient identifiable even if explicit identifiers are reduced.
assumptions: The transferred or retrievable dataset includes rich clinical/genetic context or rare-condition information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; identifiability may arise from content and metadata together.

title: Secondary use by clinician beyond the original context of availability
description: Once retrieved with additional input and analysis, the Clinician may use the context-relevant research data for purposes beyond the patient-care or originally intended context, such as broader research, teaching, or unrelated decision-making.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and downstream use controls are not strictly enforced at the clinician side.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort for downstream use/analysis after receipt.

title: Excessive inference or re-disclosure after clinician analysis
description: The Clinician's additional input and analysis may generate new sensitive inferences or summaries that reveal more about the patient or relatives than the originally shared context, and these outputs may then be further disclosed.
assumptions: Clinician-side analysis can derive additional hereditary, familial, or prognostic insights from the received data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to analysis-derived disclosure; exact PANOPTIC sub-activity uncertain.

title: Processing without sufficient patient awareness or consent alignment
description: The Clinician's retrieval and use of context-relevant research/genetic data may exceed what the patient understood or consented to, particularly where research-derived information is repurposed in clinical decision-making.
assumptions: Consent or notice may distinguish research and clinical uses, and clinician retrieval may blur that boundary.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id is best-effort; threat depends on actual consent/notice model.

title: Insufficient accountability for clinician retrieval and use
description: If retrieval, additional input, and subsequent analysis are not adequately logged or attributable, the patient may be unable to demonstrate who accessed the sensitive data and for what purpose, weakening accountability and contestability.
assumptions: Audit trails may be incomplete, inaccessible, or not granular enough for this retrieval and analysis step.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to non-repudiation/accountability concerns at the destination.

title: Residual genomic data remains on decommissioned wet lab devices
description: If privacy-relevant wet lab devices are not securely sanitized during decommissioning, residual genomic or associated personal data may remain on internal storage, buffers, logs, or removable media. Subsequent resale, reuse, servicing, or disposal could expose that data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The devices may contain persistent storage or recoverable transient data related to genomic processing.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity is best-effort; I am using PA06.02 to represent insecure disposal/decommissioning or failure to remove data before transfer/disposal.

title: Unauthorized secondary access after resale or disposal
description: A decommissioned device that still contains recoverable data can enable unauthorized parties such as resellers, refurbishers, buyers, or disposal contractors to access genomic data outside the original processing context.
assumptions: The device leaves organizational control after decommissioning and can be examined by third parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping: this is framed as unauthorized access/use enabled by improper decommissioning; PANOPTIC id may be approximate.

title: Linkability through retained identifiers and metadata on device
description: Residual sample identifiers, run metadata, user accounts, network settings, audit logs, or file naming conventions on the device may allow third parties to link records, experiments, operators, or data subjects across datasets or systems.
assumptions: The device stores operational metadata in addition to primary genomic data.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is best-effort because the exact LINDDUN Pro decomposition for linkability may vary.

title: Identifiability from residual genomic data or device metadata
description: Even if direct identifiers are absent, retained genomic sequences, sample labels, instrument logs, or configuration metadata on the decommissioned device may enable identification of individuals or laboratories when combined with other information.
assumptions: Residual data includes genomic or quasi-identifying metadata that can support re-identification.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC id and tree node are approximate best-effort mappings for re-identification risk arising from improper decommissioning.

title: Unintended disclosure of sensitive data during device decommissioning
description: Improper decommissioning can result in accidental disclosure of sensitive genomic data to parties not intended to receive it, including internal staff, disposal vendors, refurbishers, or downstream purchasers.
assumptions: Decommissioning involves handoff, transport, storage, or resale steps where unauthorized disclosure can occur.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to disclosure of information/data disclosure due to insecure disposal or transfer.

title: Residual genomic or configuration data on acquired/refurbished wet lab devices can be disclosed
description: If acquired or refurbished wet lab devices retain prior owners' genomic data, patient identifiers, run logs, calibration files, user accounts, or network configuration, storing and deploying those devices in the lab can expose sensitive data to the receiving organization or later to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The devices may contain persistent storage or embedded memory that can retain prior data after resale or refurbishment.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is best-effort based on acquisition/provisioning context; exact mapping may vary.

title: Retained device metadata may enable linkage of prior data subjects or organizations
description: Serial numbers, instrument IDs, maintenance logs, assay histories, or embedded account details left on acquired devices can be correlated with other records to link prior patients, studies, labs, or operators to the device and its data.
assumptions: The device or its software stores historical metadata that remains accessible after acquisition.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort PANOPTIC mapping; linkage is contingent on retained metadata being accessible.

title: Residual identifiers on devices may reveal identities of prior users or data subjects
description: Embedded usernames, patient IDs, sample IDs, email addresses, or service account credentials on purchased/refurbished devices can directly identify prior operators, institutions, or data subjects whose information should not accompany the device.
assumptions: The device stores directly identifying information in logs, local databases, or configuration files.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC sub-activity id is approximate.

title: Acquired devices may contain personal data beyond what is necessary for the recipient's purpose
description: When devices are obtained without verified sanitization or privacy-preserving refurbishment, the recipient may receive historical personal or sensitive data unrelated to current genomic processing needs, violating data minimization and purpose limitation expectations.
assumptions: The acquisition process does not require proof of secure wiping or privacy-focused refurbishment.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort because non-compliance categorization can vary by applicable policy/regulatory basis.

title: Lack of transparency about refurbishment/sanitization status creates unawareness of inherited privacy risk
description: If the recipient cannot determine whether a device was sourced directly from the manufacturer or refurbished according to privacy best practices, stakeholders may be unaware that residual sensitive data could be present and processed or stored on receipt.
assumptions: Procurement records or attestations about sanitization are incomplete, absent, or unreliable.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC mapping and exact unawareness node are approximate.
